summary: Follow-up T-0249 CE-1 nit: router.ts's dispatch() discarded every non-HttpError exception with ZERO server-side trace before sending the generic {code:"INTERNAL"} 500 — T-0249's live 22P02 (slug written into a UUID actor_event column) was only diagnosable via a standalone tsx repro script, because the router gave neither the client nor the server log anything but a bare INTERNAL envelope. Fix (1): a new logUnexpectedError(method, pathname, err) call, inserted at all three non-HttpError catch sites in dispatch() (async route-handler rejection, fallback sync throw, fallback async rejection) immediately BEFORE the existing sendErrorEnvelope(res,500,"INTERNAL",...) call — console.error carries the error's own message+stack (or String(err) for non-Error throws) plus method+pathname (query string and body are never read by this function). The HTTP response to the client is byte-identical to before: still the generic INTERNAL envelope, no message/stack ever crosses the wire. HttpError paths are untouched — no new logging on expected domain errors (avoids log-spam). Purely additive: 0 deleted lines in router.ts (FF-HIRE-4 additive-only), confirmed via git diff. Evaluation (2) (canonicalize the T-0249 slug→UUID adapter in src/composition/completion-effects-root.ts vs. keep it): NOT implemented — judged big/risky per the task's own instruction, written up as a standalone follow-up recommendation in spec.md §3 instead (runIssueKey's subject.subjectId is dual-purpose — PDP subject slug AND actor_event actor — so pushing resolution into runIssueKey or the ActorEventWriter contract ripples through the 420-line issue-key.test.ts's in-memory-store slug convention, t0242-entitlement-port.test.ts, both same-day T-0249 db tests, and the dormant fireCardAction path; the adapter itself is already the T-0249 r2 judge-approved shipped fix, not an unreviewed stopgap).

security_notes: logUnexpectedError never reads req headers, cookies, or the request/response body — it receives only (method, pathname-without-query-string, err) as function parameters, all already computed/thrown before it is called; there is no code path by which it could read more even if a future edit tried to pass more, since its signature is 3 primitives.

The HTTP response to the client is unchanged by this task: sendErrorEnvelope(res, 500, "INTERNAL", "internal server error") is called with the exact same literal arguments as before, on the exact same line, immediately after the new logging call — the leak-surface pinned by AC-10 (pre-existing test) and the 6 new T-0763 tests is the response body, and none of them changed shape.

HttpError paths receive no new logging — by construction only the else (non-HttpError) branch gained a call, so expected/handled errors (404, 409, 400, etc., all of which already carry an intentional, safe .message by the HttpError contract) do not start appearing in the server log where they didn't before.

A handler that itself embeds a secret into a raw Error's .message was already one console.error call away from leaking it anywhere else in this codebase (no prior discipline prevented that) — this task does not create a new class of secret-bearing surface, it stops discarding diagnostic detail a thrown Error already carried. Re-verified the existing no-secret-leak gate family (FF-583-7/FF-LP-8/FF-25/FF-1) all stay green.
